labels.notes: Partial row, unmarked, and correctly so (the ledger's exact regex finds no mark in the whole file; the bold ``**`prop:...` at ...**`` in declaration docstrings at :532 and :576 does not match it). I checked each statement against ETT.tex:1726-1749 and the strict library. (1) ModelMeasuresLocal (:108) is an honest Prop structure with the same two fields as the strict Causality.ModelMeasures (Causal/SingularGeroch.lean:174), plus 'inside every neighbourhood N'. ModelMeasuresLocal.modelMeasures (N = univ) gives the strict ModelMeasures exactly, so it is stronger. It holds at E^{1,2}, E0, E_kappa and over MassAModel, so it is not vacuous. (2) ChartIso.admissiblePastOn / admissibleFutureOn: for every open U in the chart source, a measure admissible on chartImage e U comes back to one admissible on U. No convexity hypothesis; only R1Space M, which the paper's Hausdorff (ETT.tex:254) implies. AdmissiblePastOn is the real Dieckmann structure (MeasureLocal.lean:80), so this is a genuine transfer. (3) mem_Kminus_of_intertwine needs only the continuity of the inverse on U', the two inverse laws and the matching of <=_U with <=_U'. ChartIso.symm_mem_Kminus_iff and symm_mem_Jminus_iff are the two-sided forms for A in U. Both are correct and natural. (4) le_of_causallyConvexIn_of_subset takes V an arbitrary set, causally convex in M, inside an open S. ChartIso.causallyConvexIn_source_inter_preimage concludes that e.source ∩ e⁻¹(U') is causally convex in M. ChartIso.exists_admissiblePastOn uses hSC : C.StronglyCausal, which is DEC-7's definition (Properties.lean:105, V in 𝓝 p, not necessarily open). StronglyCausalOpen is used nowhere on M, only at the model E^{1,2} inside minkowski_modelMeasuresLocal. Its conclusion also states e(U) causally convex in the model. (5) isoChartsCover_modelMeasures(Local) assume IsoChartsCover, CausallyArcConnected and StronglyCausal, with the models in local form. (6) massA_modelMeasures(Local) assume an absolutely minimal C, IsoChartsCoverDEC25 over MassAModel (any G, any singular structures of the models) and StronglyCausal; causal arc-connectedness is discharged, not assumed. massA_modelMeasures_of_natural takes IsAtlasCausalityDEC25 plus singular points in X_A-charts. (7) massA_mesure_admissible equals the strict SingularFlatAxioms.mesure_admissible with ModelMeasures discharged and IsCausal replaced by the paper's StronglyCausal. Its only hypothesis beyond the paper is SingularFlatAxioms (and the DEC-25/OQ-18 reading of E≥0-manifold). That is disclosed as strengthened, hence partial. (8) e0Manifold_* take E0Covered, IsE0Natural and StronglyCausal, plus T2, second countability and the three BTZ fields of SFALocalE0.singularFlatAxioms_iff (Causal/Port/SFALocalE0.lean:398) for the conclusion. (9) Witnesses. e0_nonvacuous checks every hypothesis of massA_mesure_admissible at E0, whose singular locus is non-empty, and derives its conclusion. e0Manifold_nonvacuous covers the E0-manifold anchors including the BTZ fields. epi_nonvacuous checks ModelMeasures at E_pi; it has no SingularFlatAxioms witness, which is disclosed. Hypothesis readings: R1Space is a weakening carried from the paper's Hausdorff, not an added hypothesis. In the conditionals T2 comes from SingularFlatAxioms.t2, and at E0-manifolds it is an instance argument. The REPORT's 'weakened' is right. Finding 1 (proof gap at ETT.tex:1734-1743) is true and correctly classified as proof-level: the proposition is not affected. Its witness is misdescribed as relatively compact in M, though; see findings.

findings.what: The witness of finding 1 is described as 'open, relatively compact, inside the chart and causally convex in M' for M = E^{1,2} ∖ {(0,0)}. It is not relatively compact in M. Its closure in M is J((-2,0),(2,0)) ∖ {(0,0)}, and (t,0) → (0,0) ∉ M; the auditor proved in Lean that no compact subset of `puncture` contains `cutDiamond`. The Lean conjunct `IsCompact (closure cutDiamond)` is the closure in E^{1,2}, so it shows that the image is relatively compact in the model. The paper's U_p is relatively compact in M, so as worded the witness does not meet every property the paper gives U_p. If this goes to the author verbatim, a false fact reaches the author and invites the reply that the witness misses a hypothesis. The finding itself stands even with relative compactness in M (by hand, not formalized; checked). Let M = E^{1,2} ∖ K, with K the closed disc {t = 0, |x| ≤ 3}. Let U_p be the union of the open diamonds I((-1.1,0),(-0.9,0)) and I((0.9,0),(1.1,0)). U_p is open, relatively compact in M (its closure lies in |t| ≥ 0.9, away from K) and inside the chart (the inclusion, chartIso_restrOpen_refl). It is causally convex in M: each diamond is convex, and no causal curve of M joins the two, because one would cross t = 0 at |x| < 1.2, inside K. Its image is not causally convex in E^{1,2}: (0,0) lies between (-1,0) and (1,0). U_p is disconnected, but the paper asks no connectedness.

findings.what: The suggested wording keeps 'Lemma restriction_convexe turns properties 3 and 4 of the model into properties 3 and 4 of U''. The prop:mesure_admissible row already carries T-ett-measures-e0's finding that restriction_convexe gives property 4 but not bare property 3, which needs its local form (pos_past_inter, kb 0148). Both findings amend the same sentence (ETT.tex:1742-1743). They are independent: this one is about whether the set is causally convex in the model, so that the lemma applies at all; T-ett-measures-e0's is about what the lemma then delivers. Curated as two separate wordings, they would contradict each other. On its own point the wording is sound: U' causally convex in E_kappa exists inside φ(V) because the models are strongly causal, and U_p = φ⁻¹(U') is causally convex in M. That second step uses M's causal arc-connectedness, which the wording should name.

observations: The import of Causal.Port.SFALocalE0, beyond the three the dispatch allowed, is acceptable for a Remarks-layer module. Causal/Remarks modules import Causal.Port modules routinely: MassADEC25 imports Port.E0Axioms and Port.E0SingularFlat, and MassAModelsInstance imports Port.E0GXStructure and Port.BPrimeE0. SFALocalE0 imports only Causal.SFATransfer and Causal.Port.BPrimeE0, which is already in the closure through MassAModelsInstance, so the import closure grows by one strict, graduated module. There is no cycle. The block's own route names E0Covered and IsE0Natural from that module.

Finding 1 versus T-ett-measures-e0's finding, so the master does not duplicate them. Both concern the step 'Lemma restriction_convexe turns properties 3 and 4 of the model into properties 3 and 4 of U_p'. T-ett-measures-e0's (already in paper_findings) is about the output: once applied to a set causally convex in the model, the lemma carries property 4 but not bare property 3. This one is about the input: the lemma must be applied in the model to φ(U_p), and the U_p chosen at l.1734-1736 (causally convex in M) need not have φ(U_p) causally convex in the model. Neither fix implies the other. Record both as separate entries, cross-referenced, with one combined suggested wording.

Hypothesis (i) of the proof, ModelMeasures, now holds at every strongly causal E≥0-manifold (DEC-7's StronglyCausal), for every absolutely minimal causality with an isomorphic chart at each point (IsoChartsCoverDEC25 over MassAModel, any G, any singular structures of the models: massA_modelMeasures; the natural one: massA_modelMeasures_of_natural). It holds in local form, inside every neighbourhood (ModelMeasuresLocal, massA_modelMeasuresLocal). At E₀-manifolds with their natural causality: e0Manifold_modelMeasures. U = φ⁻¹(U′) is then causally convex in M (ChartIso.causallyConvexIn_source_inter_preimage, by causal arc-connectedness, le_of_causallyConvexIn_of_subset). Witnesses with a singular point: e0_nonvacuous (every hypothesis of massA_mesure_admissible at E₀, and its conclusion), e0Manifold_nonvacuous, epi_nonvacuous (ModelMeasures at E_π). Family instances instMeasurableSpaceMassAModel and instBorelSpaceMassAModel, by cases on o: rfl to E₀'s ℝ × ℂ and to E_κ's ℝ × Cone κ (MeasuresEAlpha.instMeasurableSpaceCone). prop:mesure_admissible.paper_findings_append: ETT.tex:1734-1743, proof-level, distinct from the property-3 finding above. That one is about what lem:restriction_convexe delivers once the set is causally convex in the model; this one is about whether it is. « Strong causality provides a relatively compact open neighbourhood U_p of p, causally convex in M and contained in a chart with model E_κ », then « Lemma restriction_convexe turns properties 3 and 4 of the model into properties 3 and 4 of U_p ». Applied in the model, the lemma needs φ(U_p) causally convex in E_κ, and U_p causally convex in M does not give it. Lean witness: Causal.MeasuresManifolds.cutDiamond_separates. Take M = E^{1,2} ∖ {(0,0)}, the chart the inclusion (a chart isomorphism), and U_p the open diamond I((−2,0),(2,0)) with its centre removed. U_p is open, inside the chart and causally convex in M, with compact closure in E^{1,2}. Its image is not causally convex in E^{1,2}, since (0,0) lies between (−1,0) and (1,0). That U_p is not relatively compact in M, because its closure in M misses the centre. The paper's relative compactness does not save the step (by hand, not formalized). Take M = E^{1,2} ∖ K, with K the closed disc {t = 0, |x| ≤ 3}, and U_p the union of the open diamonds I((−1.1,0),(−0.9,0)) and I((0.9,0),(1.1,0)). U_p is open, relatively compact in M and inside the chart (the inclusion). It is causally convex in M: no causal curve of M joins the two diamonds, because one would cross t = 0 at |x| < 1.2. Its image is not causally convex in E^{1,2}, again because (0,0) lies between (−1,0) and (1,0). The proposition is not affected. Choose U′ causally convex in the model first and put U_p = φ⁻¹(U′), which is causally convex in M by strong causality and causal arc-connectedness of M (ChartIso.causallyConvexIn_source_inter_preimage). The chart carries the measure back with no convexity (ChartIso.admissiblePastOn). Suggested wording for l.1734-1743, which also takes in the property-3 finding above: « Strong causality provides a neighbourhood V of p, causally convex in M and contained in a chart φ with model E_κ. Let U′ ⊂ φ(V) be a relatively compact open neighbourhood of φ(p), causally convex in E_κ, and U_p = φ^{-1}(U′). Since V is causally convex in M and M is causally arc-connected, x ≤ y ≤ z in M with x, z ∈ U_p gives φ(x) ≤ φ(y) ≤ φ(z) in E_κ, so U_p is causally convex in M. [...] Restricted to the relatively compact U′ these measures are finite, so property 2 holds too. Lemma restriction_convexe turns property 4 of the model into property 4 of U′. Property 3 holds on U′ since J⁻(q) ∖ J⁻(p) (resp. J⁺(p) ∖ J⁺(q)) meets every neighbourhood of q (resp. p) in a non-empty open set or, in the past at a BTZ point, in a segment of the singular line. The chart φ carries properties 1 to 4 from U′ to U_p. »
